Disney+ is the most politically contentious streaming platform in America right now. When parents search for what to watch with their kids, Disney+ sits in an awkward middle ground between beloved classics and new releases that have sparked national debates. This list ranks every Disney+ title in VirtueVigil's database by net woke score. Decide for yourself what that means for your family's watch list.

Rankings are sorted by net woke score (Woke Score minus Traditional Score), highest to lowest. Positive numbers indicate woke lean. Negative numbers indicate traditional lean.

#1 — Strange World (2022)

STRONGLY WOKEWOKE: 27.5TRAD: 12.32NET: +15.18 WOKE

Genre: Animation/Adventure • Platform: Disney+

The most ideologically concentrated Disney+ title in VirtueVigil's database by net score. Features Disney's first openly gay teen protagonist and builds its family adventure around progressive environmental and identity themes. Net woke plus 15.18. A deliberate statement. The film was a notable box office disappointment; its ideological content is widely cited as a contributing factor among conservative family audiences who opted out.

Read the full VirtueVigil review

#2 — Turning Red (2022)

STRONGLY WOKEWOKE: 17.85TRAD: 4.55NET: +13.3 WOKE

Genre: Animation • Platform: Disney+

Net woke plus 13.3. A trad score of 4.55 against a woke score of 17.85 reflects almost no traditional counterweight. Turning Red frames coming-of-age as a rejection of parental control and traditional family expectations. The film's sympathies are entirely with the child's rebellion and entirely against the mother's traditional values. One of the most explicit ideological statements in Pixar's catalog.

Read the full VirtueVigil review

#3 — Zootopia (2016)

STRONGLY WOKEWOKE: 21.48TRAD: 12.32NET: +9.16 WOKE

Genre: Animation • Platform: Disney+

Net woke plus 9.16. Built its entire narrative around a systemic racism allegory presented to children as universal truth. The implicit argument (institutional bias against predators equals real-world racial bias against minorities) is never made explicit in ways a young child would identify, which makes it more effective as ideological communication, not less. Well-made animation. Fully intentional ideology.

#4 — Wish (2023)

WOKEWOKE: 17.45TRAD: 11.9NET: +5.55 WOKE

Genre: Animation • Platform: Disney+

Net woke plus 5.55. Disney's centennial celebration film uses its fairy tale premise to frame individual empowerment against institutional control, with the authoritarian villain representing a specific type of paternalistic traditional authority. Consistent with the newer Disney tradition of positioning traditional power structures as the obstacle to authentic self-expression.

#5 — Mulan (2020)

MIXEDWOKE: 20.78TRAD: 17.64NET: +3.14 WOKE

Genre: Action/Adventure • Platform: Disney+

Net woke plus 3.14. High raw scores on both sides. The traditional score (17.64) comes from its Chinese cultural setting, filial piety themes, and honor-based value system. The woke score (20.78) comes from its feminist framing and the Western progressive lens applied to a traditional story. The film uses traditional values as set dressing while delivering a contemporary feminist argument. Also notable for its production amid Xinjiang controversy.

The Disney+ Verdict for Conservative Parents

The split on this list is stark and instructive. The top five entries (Strange World through Wish) represent Disney's deliberate push into explicitly progressive family content. Strange World at plus 15.18 and Turning Red at plus 13.3 are not films that accidentally contain progressive elements. They are films built around progressive arguments delivered to children.

The bottom half tells a different story. Soul, Coco, Spider-Man: No Way Home, and The Greatest Showman represent the platform's strongest traditionally-aligned content. These films deliver messages about family, sacrifice, heritage, and purpose that resonate with conservative values.
